songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: Blazing Eleven, tight Caution>Feedback and soaring Garcia tones
ai_show_review.blurb: Features an incendiary The Eleven and a relentless Alligator jam, capped by a crisp Caution → Feedback sequence. Jerry’s guitar is on fire throughout while Phil anchors the improvisations with resonant bass lines.
ai_show_review.review: The February 12, 1969 Fillmore East show captures the Dead at a creative peak, rolling from a powerful Dark Star into Saint Stephen and then launching into one of the most electric renditions of The Eleven ever recorded. Garcia’s Fender Twin roars, especially on The Eleven and during the soaring leads in Killer Dupree, while Phil Lesh weaves geometric bass lines that lock perfectly with the twin‑drum assault of Mickey and Bill. The first set builds relentless momentum, culminating in a blistering Alligator jam that segues into an immaculate Caution → Feedback sequence – the low A feedback note provides a cello‑like backbone that lets the keyboards breathe while the drums stay crystal clear. The band’s energy never wanes, delivering a high‑octane performance that remains one of the late‑‘69 highlights for any Deadhead looking to hear the group in top form.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with superb fidelity, clear instrument separation and minimal tape artifacts.

key_highlights: The Eleven – fiery guitar work and geometric bass interplay
Alligator jam with relentless drive and tight dual‑drum foundation
Caution → Feedback sequence showcases dynamic keyboard texture and crisp drum separation
Partial Dark Star sets the tone for a high‑energy set

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is on fire – roaring Twin on The Eleven, soaring leads on Killer Dupree and a heavy‑metal crunch at the end of Caution.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh is "in all the right places", delivering deep, resonant bass that drives the jams and adds harmonic geometry throughout.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are crystal clear; Mickey’s percussion blends tightly with Bill, providing a solid rhythmic backbone.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is tight and well‑mixed, contributing to the powerful dual‑drum sound that propels the set.
